response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.throws, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), s AS (SELECT throws, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT throws, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM a WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: player.player_id is unique, so the inner join does not duplicate award rows. NULL throws forms its own group via GROUP BY. The 'average share across hands' is the mean of shares over all groups, including the NULL group, before filtering.
